name: Unakoti Heritage Site (Rock Carvings)
description: Ancient open-air gallery of colossal rock-cut sculptures and bas-reliefs of Hindu deities, primarily Shaivite, carved into the hillsides of Unakoti. Centerpiece is the ~30-foot Unakotiswara Kal Bhairava (Shiva head). Dates to 7th-9th century CE; UNESCO Tentative World Heritage Site since 2022. Also known as Subrai Khung.
facts: Name means 'one less than a crore' from local legend of 99,99,999 carvings
About 8 km east of Kailashahar, 178 km from Agartala
Annual Ashokastami Mela attracts thousands of pilgrims
ASI protected site with streams and forested setting

name: Kailashahar Town
description: District headquarters of Unakoti and historic former capital of the Tripuri kingdom. Gateway town on the banks of the Manu River near the Bangladesh border, serving as base for Unakoti rock carvings and local lakes/temples. Known for markets and as entry point to northern Tripura attractions.
facts: Headquarters of Unakoti district (formed 2012 from North Tripura)
Elevation around 28-32 metres
Nearest town to Unakoti site (~8 km)
Connected by road and near Kumarghat railway

name: Khowrabil Lake (Rajar Dighi)
description: Historic lake near Kailashahar in Unakoti district, popular for annual traditional water festival with boat races in October-November. Surrounded by scenic areas and close to Chaturdas Devata Mandir; draws visitors for water sports potential and natural setting.
facts: About 7 km from Kailashahar
Annual boat race during water festival
Also known as Rajar Dighi
Near Chaturdas Devata Mandir

name: Unakoti Eco Park
description: Developed eco-park adjacent to the Unakoti rock carvings site, offering walking trails, green spaces, and views of the forested hills and sculptures. Complements the heritage visit with nature relaxation amid the Unakoti landscape.
facts: Located near the entrance to Unakoti Heritage Site
Provides pathways and picnic spots
Part of tourism development around the rock carvings
Surrounded by lush vegetation and streams

name: Chaturdas Devata Mandir
description: Historic temple near Khowrabil Lake in Kailashahar area, linked to the ancient capital history of the region as per Rajmala texts. Attracts devotees and visitors exploring Unakoti district's spiritual sites.
facts: Close to Khowrabil Lake
Associated with ancient janapath history of Kailashahar
Part of local pilgrimage circuit
Mentioned in district tourism listings

name: Jampui Hills
description: Highest hill range in Tripura at about 3,000 ft, known as the Eternal Hills of Spring and Orchid Paradise of India. Features orange orchards, dense forests, mild climate, Mizo/Lushai culture, and panoramic views toward Mizoram and Bangladesh.
facts: Average elevation around 1000 metres
Home to over 50 orchid species including Vanda coerulea
Annual Orange Festival in November
About 200 km from Agartala, 70 km from Dharmanagar

name: Betlingchhip Peak (Thaidawr)
description: Highest peak in Tripura at 930 metres in the Jampui Hills. Offers 360-degree panoramic views of Mizoram hills, Chittagong Hill Tracts in Bangladesh, and surrounding valleys. Accessible via short trek from the ridge near Vanghmun.
facts: Also known as Thaidawr or Betalongchhip
Highest point in the state of Tripura
Watchtower present for views
Best visited for sunrise and clear weather

name: Vanghmun Village
description: Hilltop village in Jampui Hills, known as the cleanest village in Tripura. Gateway to Betlingchhip Peak, with Mizo culture, homestays, Eden Tourist Lodge, and orange orchards. Offers authentic community tourism experiences.
facts: Headquarters of Jampui Hills block
About 220 km from Agartala
Eden Tourist Lodge located here
Popular base for hill treks and festivals

name: Shilchhara Buddha Waterfall
description: Tranquil hidden waterfall near Pecharthal in lush forest setting. Cascading waters amid dense greenery offer a peaceful nature escape, popular for walks and quiet immersion away from crowds.
facts: Located near Pecharthal town
Also referred to as Pecharthal or Silcherra Waterfall
Set in forested area with cave features nearby
Accessible by local transport from Pecharthal

name: Rowa Wildlife Sanctuary
description: Compact wildlife sanctuary near Panisagar covering about 0.86 sq km, established in 1988. Rich in birds, primates, reptiles, and mixed forests; ideal for short birdwatching and nature walks despite small size.
facts: Established in 1988
Area approximately 85-86 hectares
Near Panisagar, about 18-23 km from Dharmanagar
Home to barking deer, macaques, and diverse bird species

name: Kalibari Temple (Dharmanagar)
description: Prominent Kali temple in Dharmanagar town, a key spiritual and cultural center for the district. Draws devotees for festivals like Kali Puja and Navratri, with nearby Dighi pond and local markets.
facts: Central temple in Dharmanagar town
Site of major Kali Puja and Agomoni celebrations
Located near Kalibari Road and town Dighi
Focal point for community gatherings

name: Dharmanagar Town
description: District headquarters of North Tripura and main gateway town near the Bangladesh border. Serves as base for Jampui Hills, Rowa Sanctuary, and other northern attractions, with markets, railway station, and mild climate.
facts: Headquarters of North Tripura district
Nearest railway station for Jampui Hills (~70 km)
Elevation around 32 metres
Connected by road and rail to Agartala and Assam
